```{python}
#| label: setup
import importlib.util
import json
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import altair as alt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display


def find_root() -> Path:
    here = Path.cwd().resolve()
    for candidate in (here, *here.parents):
        if (candidate / "_quarto.yml").exists():
            return candidate
    msg = "Run from inside the bdsurv project (no _quarto.yml found)."
    raise FileNotFoundError(msg)


ROOT = find_root()
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "bench_method_comparison", ROOT / "scripts" / "bench_method_comparison.py"
)
bench = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
sys.modules["bench_method_comparison"] = bench
_spec.loader.exec_module(bench)
_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "method_comparison_charts", ROOT / "scripts" / "method_comparison_charts.py"
)
charts = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
sys.modules["method_comparison_charts"] = charts
_spec.loader.exec_module(charts)

LAMBDA = bench.LAMBDA
DATA = ROOT / "benchmarks" / "data"
DRAFT = not (DATA / bench.ROWS_FILE).exists()
if DRAFT:
    # No committed results yet: run the tiny draft grid so the page still renders.
    _tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    bench.main(
        ["--quick", "--shards-dir", str(_tmp / "shards"), "--data-dir", str(_tmp / "data")]
    )
    DATA = _tmp / "data"

rows = pd.read_csv(DATA / bench.ROWS_FILE)
units = pd.read_csv(DATA / bench.UNITS_FILE)
env = json.loads((DATA / bench.ENV_FILE).read_text())

LABEL_CONTOUR = charts.LABEL_CONTOUR
LABEL_RUN = charts.LABEL_RUN
LABEL_KEPT = charts.LABEL_KEPT
PALETTE = charts.PALETTE
MUS = sorted(rows["mu"].unique())
TS = sorted(rows["T"].unique())
N_REPS = int(rows.groupby(["method", "mu", "T"]).size().min())
N_CELLS = rows.groupby(["mu", "T"]).ngroups
```

## What is compared

Both methods sample a birth-death tree that **survives to time $T$**.
The birth rate is fixed at $\lambda = 1$ and the death rate $\mu$ runs from
$0.6$ (supercritical) through $1$ (critical) to $20$ (highly subcritical), on a
grid of `{python} len(MUS)` rates; the terminal time $T$ runs from $1$ to $100$ on a
grid of `{python} len(TS)` values.

- **Contour process** builds one tree that survives by construction.
  It is exact and works for any rates.
- **Multilevel splitting** evolves a swarm of particles and clones the ones still
  alive at each level.
  A run returns several trees, but clones of one survivor share their history, so
  the kept trees are **not independent**.
  It accepts any positive rates.
  When $\Pr(\text{survive to } T) > 0.5$ (always so for $\mu/\lambda < 0.5$) there
  is nothing to split, and it simulates trees one at a time until one survives.

Splitting is charged two ways.
*Per independent tree* bills a whole run for a single tree, which is the fair
price when independence matters.
*Per kept tree* divides the run by the number of trees it kept, which is the
optimistic view.

Each point is the **mean** over independent replicates (at least
`{python} N_REPS` per method and cell, across `{python} N_CELLS` cells), and the
shaded band is a 95% confidence interval for the mean (normal approximation).
Both axes of the cost charts are logarithmic.
Click a legend entry to show only that method (shift-click to add more,
double-click to reset).

::: {.callout-note}
A cell $(\mu, T)$ is skipped when the expected tree size given survival,
$e^{(\lambda-\mu)T} / \Pr(T)$, exceeds
`{python} f"{bench.MAX_EXPECTED_POPULATION:,.0f}"` individuals.
Supercritical trees grow exponentially, so this only trims the longest horizons
for $\mu < 1$.
:::

```{python}
#| label: curves
rows["per_kept"] = np.where(rows["n_trees"] > 0, rows["seconds"] / rows["n_trees"], np.nan)
split_rows = rows[rows["method"] == "splitting"]
curves = charts.curves_from_rows(rows)


def regime(mu: float) -> str:
    if mu < LAMBDA:
        return (
            f"supercritical: a tree survives forever with probability "
            f"{1 - mu / LAMBDA:.2f}"
        )
    if mu == LAMBDA:
        return "critical"
    return "subcritical: survival to large $T$ is rare"


X_BY_T = charts.x_by_t(TS)
X_BY_MU = charts.x_by_mu(MUS)


def cost_chart(data: pd.DataFrame, x: alt.X, **kwargs) -> alt.Chart:
    return charts.cost_chart(data, x, lam=LAMBDA, statistic="mean", **kwargs)


diagnostics = (
    split_rows.groupby(["mu", "T"])
    .agg(
        trees=("n_trees", "median"),
        attempts=("n_attempts", "median"),
        levels=("levels", "median"),
    )
    .reset_index()
)


def diagnostic_chart(mu: float) -> alt.Chart:
    data = diagnostics[diagnostics["mu"] == mu]
    panels = []
    for column, title in [
        ("trees", "trees kept per run"),
        ("attempts", "attempts per run"),
        ("levels", "levels"),
    ]:
        panels.append(
            alt.Chart(data)
            .mark_line(strokeWidth=3, point=alt.OverlayMarkDef(size=60, filled=True))
            .encode(
                x=alt.X(
                    "T:Q",
                    scale=alt.Scale(type="log"),
                    title="terminal time T (log scale)",
                    axis=alt.Axis(format="g", values=[1, 10, 100]),
                ),
                y=alt.Y(f"{column}:Q", scale=alt.Scale(zero=True), title=title),
                tooltip=[alt.Tooltip("T:Q", format="g"), f"{column}:Q"],
                color=alt.value(PALETTE[LABEL_KEPT]),
            )
            .properties(width=270, height=220, title=title)
        )
    return alt.hconcat(*panels)


def show_mu(mu: float) -> None:
    if mu not in set(curves["mu"]):
        display(Markdown(f"No data for $\\mu = {mu:g}$ in this results file."))
        return
    top_t = max(curves.loc[curves["mu"] == mu, "T"])
    display(
        Markdown(
            f"$\\lambda = 1$, $\\mu = {mu:g}$: {regime(mu)}. "
            f"Benchmarked up to $T = {top_t:.3g}$."
        )
    )
    display(cost_chart(curves[curves["mu"] == mu], X_BY_T))
    display(Markdown("**How splitting behaved**"))
    display(diagnostic_chart(mu))


def show_t(t: float) -> None:
    data = curves[np.isclose(curves["T"], t)]
    if data.empty:
        display(Markdown(f"No data for $T = {t:g}$ in this results file."))
        return
    display(
        Markdown(
            f"$\\lambda = 1$, $T = {t:g}$. "
            f"Benchmarked $\\mu$ from {data['mu'].min():g} to {data['mu'].max():g}."
        )
    )
    display(cost_chart(data, X_BY_MU, mark_critical=True))
```

## Where does each method win?

The ratio of splitting (per independent tree) to the contour process, for every
cell that was benchmarked.
Above 1 the contour process is cheaper.

```{python}
#| label: ratio
wide = curves.pivot_table(index=["mu", "T"], columns="method", values="mean").reset_index()
wide["ratio"] = wide[LABEL_RUN] / wide[LABEL_CONTOUR]
heat = wide.dropna(subset=["ratio"]).copy()
heat["T_label"] = heat["T"].map(lambda t: f"{t:g}")
(
    alt.Chart(heat)
    .mark_rect()
    .encode(
        x=alt.X(
            "T_label:O",
            sort=[f"{t:g}" for t in TS],
            title="terminal time T",
            axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0),
        ),
        y=alt.Y("mu:O", sort="descending", title="death rate μ"),
        color=alt.Color(
            "ratio:Q",
            scale=alt.Scale(type="log", scheme="viridis"),
            legend=alt.Legend(title="splitting / contour", format="~g"),
        ),
        tooltip=[
            "mu:O",
            alt.Tooltip("T:Q", format="g"),
            alt.Tooltip("ratio:Q", format=".3g"),
        ],
    )
    .properties(width=900, height=460)
)
```

## Random numbers drawn

Time depends on the machine and on bookkeeping.
A machine-independent measure of the stochastic work is the number of random
numbers drawn, counted by `bdsurv.count_draws` in an untimed pass
(`scripts/count_draws.py`) that reuses the benchmark seeds.
Counted runs produce the same trees as the timed ones.
Splitting also copies every particle's records when it clones it; that costs
time but no draws, so draws understate its cost.
The draw counts cover the same constant-rate grid as the timings, with fewer replicates.

```{python}
#| label: draws
DRAWS = DATA / "draws.csv"
HAVE_DRAWS = DRAWS.exists()
if not HAVE_DRAWS:
    display(
        Markdown(
            "No draw counts yet: run `uv run python scripts/count_draws.py` "
            "(or shard it with `--shard i/N`, then `--merge`)."
        )
    )
else:
    draws = pd.read_csv(DRAWS)
    draws = draws[draws["model"] == "constant"]
    draw_curves = charts.curves_from_draws(draws)
    draw_mus = sorted(draw_curves["mu"].unique())
    draw_ts = sorted(draw_curves["T"].unique())

    def draws_chart(data: pd.DataFrame, x: alt.X, title: str, *, critical: bool) -> alt.Chart:
        base = alt.Chart(data).encode(x=x, color=charts.color_encoding())
        y_title = "mean random numbers drawn per tree (log scale)"
        y = alt.Y("mean:Q", scale=alt.Scale(type="log"), title=y_title)
        tooltip = [
            "method",
            alt.Tooltip(x.shorthand, format="g"),
            alt.Tooltip("mean:Q", format=",.0f", title="mean draws"),
            alt.Tooltip("ci_lo:Q", format=",.0f", title="95% CI low"),
            alt.Tooltip("ci_hi:Q", format=",.0f", title="95% CI high"),
            "replicates",
        ]
        area = base.mark_area(opacity=0.15).encode(
            y=alt.Y("ci_lo:Q", scale=alt.Scale(type="log"), title=y_title), y2="ci_hi:Q"
        )
        line = base.mark_line(strokeWidth=3).encode(y=y)
        points = base.mark_point(size=70, filled=True).encode(y=y, tooltip=tooltip)
        layers = [area, line, points]
        if critical:
            layers.append(
                alt.Chart(pd.DataFrame({"mu": [LAMBDA]}))
                .mark_rule(strokeDash=[6, 4], color="#888888")
                .encode(x="mu:Q")
            )
        return alt.layer(*layers).properties(width=900, height=380, title=title)

    X_DRAWS_BY_MU = alt.X(
        "mu:Q",
        scale=alt.Scale(type="log", nice=False, padding=12),
        title="death rate μ (log scale)",
        axis=alt.Axis(values=[float(m) for m in draw_mus], format="g", labelOverlap=True),
    )
    X_DRAWS_BY_T = alt.X(
        "T:Q",
        scale=alt.Scale(type="log", nice=False, padding=12),
        title="terminal time T (log scale)",
        axis=alt.Axis(values=[float(t) for t in draw_ts], format="g", labelOverlap=True),
    )
```

Points are the mean over replicates and the band is a 95% confidence interval for
the mean.
Both axes are logarithmic.

## Are the trees right?

For a linear birth-death process from one individual, the number alive at $T$ given
survival is **geometric** on $\{1, 2, \dots\}$ with mean
$e^{(\lambda-\mu)T} / \Pr(\text{survive to } T)$.
Each replicate records the population of one tree, so the two methods can be
checked against this exact law with a one-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov (KS)
distance.
For splitting only one randomly chosen tree per run is used, so the draws are
independent.

```{python}
#| label: agreement


def exact_mean(mu: float, terminal_time: float) -> float:
    return bench.expected_population(mu, terminal_time)


def ks_distance(sample: np.ndarray, mean: float) -> float:
    support = np.arange(1, int(sample.max()) + 1)
    empirical = np.searchsorted(np.sort(sample), support, side="right") / len(sample)
    exact = 1.0 - (1.0 - 1.0 / mean) ** support
    return float(np.max(np.abs(empirical - exact)))


LABEL_SPLIT_AGREE = "Splitting (one tree per run)"
records = []
for (method, mu, t), frame in rows.dropna(subset=["pop_at_T"]).groupby(
    ["method", "mu", "T"]
):
    sample = frame["pop_at_T"].to_numpy(dtype=int)
    records.append(
        {
            "method": LABEL_CONTOUR if method == "contour" else LABEL_SPLIT_AGREE,
            "mu": mu,
            "T": t,
            "n": len(sample),
            "ks": ks_distance(sample, exact_mean(mu, t)),
            "critical": 1.36 / np.sqrt(len(sample)),
        }
    )
agreement = pd.DataFrame(records)
agreement["flagged"] = agreement["ks"] > agreement["critical"]

agree_color = alt.Color(
    "method:N",
    scale=alt.Scale(
        domain=[LABEL_CONTOUR, LABEL_SPLIT_AGREE],
        range=[PALETTE[LABEL_CONTOUR], PALETTE[LABEL_RUN]],
    ),
    legend=alt.Legend(title=None, orient="bottom", labelFontSize=14),
)
x_axis = alt.X(
    "T:Q",
    scale=alt.Scale(type="log"),
    title="terminal time T (log scale)",
    axis=alt.Axis(format="g", values=[1, 10, 100]),
)
lines = (
    alt.Chart()
    .mark_line(strokeWidth=2.5, point=alt.OverlayMarkDef(size=45, filled=True))
    .encode(
        x=x_axis,
        y=alt.Y("ks:Q", scale=alt.Scale(zero=True), title="KS distance"),
        color=agree_color,
        tooltip=[
            "method",
            "mu:Q",
            alt.Tooltip("T:Q", format="g"),
            alt.Tooltip("ks:Q", format=".4f"),
            "n",
        ],
    )
)
threshold = (
    alt.Chart()
    .transform_filter(alt.datum.method == LABEL_CONTOUR)
    .mark_line(color="#888888", strokeDash=[5, 4])
    .encode(x=x_axis, y="critical:Q")
)
(
    alt.layer(lines, threshold, data=agreement)
    .properties(width=260, height=190)
    .facet(
        facet=alt.Facet("mu:O", title="death rate μ", header=alt.Header(labelFontSize=14)),
        columns=3,
    )
)
```

The dashed line is the 5% critical value $1.36/\sqrt{n}$ for a continuous law;
it is conservative for this discrete one.
With many cells, a few exceedances are expected by chance even for a correct
sampler.

```{python}
#| label: agreement-table
summary = (
    agreement.groupby("method")
    .agg(
        cells=("ks", "size"),
        flagged=("flagged", "sum"),
        median_ks=("ks", "median"),
        max_ks=("ks", "max"),
    )
    .reset_index()
)
summary["share flagged"] = summary["flagged"] / summary["cells"]
summary.rename(
    columns={
        "cells": "cells checked",
        "flagged": "cells above 5% line",
        "median_ks": "median KS",
        "max_ks": "max KS",
    }
).style.hide(axis="index").format(
    {"median KS": "{:.4f}", "max KS": "{:.4f}", "share flagged": "{:.1%}"}
)
```

### Cells above the line

```{python}
#| label: flagged-cells
flagged = agreement[agreement["flagged"]].copy()
if flagged.empty:
    display(Markdown("No cell exceeds the 5% line."))
else:
    flagged["exact mean"] = [exact_mean(m, t) for m, t in zip(flagged["mu"], flagged["T"])]
    flagged["sample mean"] = [
        float(
            rows[
                (rows["mu"] == m)
                & (rows["T"] == t)
                & (rows["method"] == ("contour" if lab == LABEL_CONTOUR else "splitting"))
            ]["pop_at_T"].mean()
        )
        for lab, m, t in zip(flagged["method"], flagged["mu"], flagged["T"])
    ]
    display(
        flagged[["method", "mu", "T", "n", "ks", "critical", "sample mean", "exact mean"]]
        .rename(columns={"mu": "μ", "ks": "KS", "critical": "5% line"})
        .style.hide(axis="index")
        .format(
            {"μ": "{:g}", "T": "{:.3g}", "KS": "{:.3f}", "5% line": "{:.3f}",
             "sample mean": "{:.2f}", "exact mean": "{:.2f}"}
        )
    )
```

With `{python} N_REPS` replicates per cell the test has little power, so a flagged
cell is a prompt to rerun it with more replicates, not evidence of a bias.

replicates; the shaded bands show it.

## Takeaways

```{python}
#| label: takeaways
c = curves[curves["method"] == LABEL_CONTOUR]
k = curves[curves["method"] == LABEL_KEPT]

lines_out = []
fastest, slowest = c.loc[c["mean"].idxmin()], c.loc[c["mean"].idxmax()]
lines_out.append(
    f"- **Contour process:** mean cost per tree runs from "
    f"{fastest['mean'] * 1e3:.2g} ms (μ = {fastest['mu']:g}, T = {fastest['T']:g}) "
    f"to {slowest['mean']:.2g} s (μ = {slowest['mu']:g}, T = {slowest['T']:g})."
)
if not heat.empty:
    lo, hi = heat.loc[heat["ratio"].idxmin()], heat.loc[heat["ratio"].idxmax()]
    share = float((heat["ratio"] > 1).mean())
    lines_out.append(
        f"- **Splitting, per set of trees** costs between {lo['ratio']:.2g}× "
        f"(μ = {lo['mu']:g}, T = {lo['T']:g}) and {hi['ratio']:.2g}× "
        f"(μ = {hi['mu']:g}, T = {hi['T']:g}) the contour process; the contour "
        f"process is cheaper in {share:.0%} of the {len(heat)} cells."
    )
    merged = pd.merge(
        k[["mu", "T", "mean"]],
        c[["mu", "T", "mean"]],
        on=["mu", "T"],
        suffixes=("_kept", "_contour"),
    )
    cheaper = float((merged["mean_kept"] < merged["mean_contour"]).mean())
    lines_out.append(
        f"- **Splitting, per kept tree** is cheaper than the contour process in "
        f"{cheaper:.0%} of cells, but those trees are correlated."
    )
flag = agreement.groupby("method")["flagged"].mean()
lines_out.append(
    "- **Accuracy:** share of cells where the KS distance exceeds the 5% line: "
    + "; ".join(f"{name}, {share:.0%}" for name, share in flag.items())
    + "."
)
display(Markdown("\n".join(lines_out)))
```
